Constrained Delaunay triangulation with refinement (CDT backend)

Source: R/cdt.R
cdt_triangulate.Rd

Thin binding to the artem-ogre/CDT library. Input mirrors RTriangle::pslg: vertices as x/y and constraint segments as index pairs into the vertices.

Usage

cdt_triangulate(
  x,
  y,
  s0 = NULL,
  s1 = NULL,
  max_area = NULL,
  min_angle = NULL,
  max_steiner = Inf,
  min_edge_length = NULL,
  min_edge_frac = 0.3,
  area_edge_frac = 0.25,
  conforming = FALSE,
  erase = c("outer", "hull", "holes"),
  intersect = c("resolve", "error", "ignore"),
  angle_first = FALSE,
  depth_distinct = FALSE,
  edge_sources = FALSE
)

Arguments

x, y

vertex coordinates

s0, s1

1-based vertex indices of constraint segment start/end (may be NULL)

max_area

maximum triangle area (Ruppert refinement by area), NULL for none

min_angle

minimum triangle angle in degrees, NULL for none

max_steiner

budget of Steiner points to insert (Inf for unlimited)

min_edge_length

refinement does not split edges or triangles already shorter than this. NULL (the default) chooses a value from the input and the targets (see default_min_edge_length()): a fraction of the median constraint segment length, capped so that it never blocks the max_area target. This stops the refiner cascading into sharp input corners. Use 0 to never give up.

min_edge_frac

fraction of the median constraint segment length used when min_edge_length is NULL

area_edge_frac

fraction of sqrt(max_area) that caps the default floor

conforming

if TRUE use conforming (Steiner on segments) instead of constrained

erase

one of "outer" (drop triangles outside the segment-bounded region, as RTriangle's -p does), "hull" (keep the convex hull), "holes" (also drop even-depth regions). With no segments there is no boundary, so "hull" is used.

intersect

how crossing constraints are handled: "resolve" inserts the crossing point, "error" fails, "ignore" skips the check

angle_first

when both criteria are given, refine by angle before area (default is area then angle; the two orderings differ little)

depth_distinct

also return depth_distinct, a per-triangle depth that counts a doubled (overlapping) boundary once rather than once per copy. The default depth counts per copy; the two differ only where the only path from outside a triangle crosses a shared, doubled boundary.

edge_sources

also return edge_sources, a data frame with one row per fixed edge and input segment covering it (see Value)

Value

list with P (vertices), T (1-based triangle indices, wound counter-clockwise / positive signed area), S (fixed edges), depth (per-triangle constraint layer depth: 0 outside, odd inside, even hole; a doubled shared boundary is counted once per copy), origin (a factor giving each vertex's provenance: "input", "crossing" or "steiner"), n_input (vertices after dedupe, before Steiner), n_crossing (vertices added resolving crossing constraints), input_map (input vertex -> deduped vertex index), min_edge_length (the value used), and unrefined, a data frame with one row per refinement pass counting what CDT could not refine (short edges, sharp fixed corners, and so on). When depth_distinct = TRUE the list also has depth_distinct (a doubled boundary counted once). When edge_sources = TRUE the list also has edge_sources, a data frame with columns edge (row in S), segment (position of the input segment in s0, s1) and forward (TRUE when the input segment runs the same way as the S row, from its first to its second vertex). Every input segment covering an edge has its own row, through crossings, splits and refinement, so an edge shared by k input segments (duplicates included) has k rows. Zero-length input segments have no rows.

Examples

## unit square with a square hole: two closed rings of 4 vertices
x <- c(0, 1, 1, 0, 0.25, 0.75, 0.75, 0.25)
y <- c(0, 0, 1, 1, 0.25, 0.25, 0.75, 0.75)
s0 <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8)
s1 <- c(2, 3, 4, 1, 6, 7, 8, 5)

## constrained triangulation, hole triangles kept with even depth
r <- cdt_triangulate(x, y, s0, s1)
table(r$depth)
#> 
#> 1 2 
#> 8 2 

## drop the hole and refine by area and minimum angle
r2 <- cdt_triangulate(x, y, s0, s1, erase = "holes",
                      max_area = 0.005, min_angle = 25)
table(r2$origin)
#> 
#>    input crossing  steiner 
#>        8        0      112 
plot(r2$P, asp = 1, pch = ".")
polygon(r2$P[t(cbind(r2$T, NA)), ], col = "grey90")


## which input segments make up each fixed edge
r4 <- cdt_triangulate(x, y, s0, s1, max_area = 0.05, edge_sources = TRUE)
head(r4$edge_sources)
#>   edge segment forward
#> 1    1       1   FALSE
#> 2    2       6    TRUE
#> 3    3       3   FALSE
#> 4    4       4    TRUE
#> 5    5       4   FALSE
#> 6    6       3    TRUE

## points only: Delaunay triangulation of the convex hull
set.seed(1)
r3 <- cdt_triangulate(runif(30), runif(30))
nrow(r3$T)
#> [1] 51
